title: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor

input.lead: It comes after the library was closed earlier this year when staff reported 'bouncy' floors
input.summary: It comes after the library was closed earlier this year when staff reported 'bouncy' floors
input.evidence_text: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor - BBC News Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, Asbestos was discovered after 'bouncy' floors triggered an investigation at Royton Library, in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago A library has been closed for urgent repairs after asbestos and contaminated debris were discovered beneath its floors. Royton Library, in Oldham, closed earlier this year after staff reported sections of flooring had become "bouncy" and inspectors found severe dry rot. Further investigations uncovered asbestos, a hazardous material once widely used in construction, beneath the building's floors the Local Democracy Reporting Service reported . According to a council report, the work is expected to take five to six weeks and is needed to address "immediate health, safety and building risks". Councillors are due to consider the plans on 19 November. Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, It comes after the library was refurbished as part of a £4m scheme which finished in 2024 The total costs of the work is not currently known and any potential costs have not been made public, according to the LDRS. The library will operate from Downey House on Church Street, in Royton, until further notice. Subnum Hariff-Khan, Oldham Council's head of heritage, libraries and arts, said in October: "We know how important Royton Library is to local residents and we're pleased to be able to continue delivering a library service while these essential repairs take place." "We'd like to thank customers for their patience and understanding while these essential works are carried out to secure the future of this important library building." title: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules

input.lead: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal
input.summary: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal
input.evidence_text: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The incidents occurred at the A&E department of the Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan, the tribunal heard By Hannah Richardson Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 17 November 2026 A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled. Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the Royal Albert Infirmary. It took into account that he had not committed the misconduct again, and that some colleagues spoke in his favour. But in overturning the tribunal's decision, Mr Justice Squires said the fact that Zeeshan "had not repeated the misconduct while under active investigation cold not be sufficient" to avoid being barred from the profession. The tribunal found Zeeshan had "exploited the health concerns of two female junior colleagues", touching them on their breasts and bottom, which it said amounted to "serious misconduct". He denied the allegations, which meant he had had "not been able to demonstrate significant insight" into his misconduct, the panel found. It could not "fully assess" the risk that he might do it again, it said. But the panel noted that by the time it was deciding how to punish him, it was five years since the incidents happened. It decided to suspend him for a year "to allow him the opportunity to show that he had developed insight into the concern identified". title: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships

input.lead: Dawud Hussain, 18, is studying to become an electrician but has yet to secure an apprenticeship
input.summary: Dawud Hussain, 18, is studying to become an electrician but has yet to secure an apprenticeship
input.evidence_text: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships - BBC News Image caption, Dawud Hussain says he has struggled to find an apprenticeship as an electrician By Haider Saleem , North West and Liv Cleal , Reporting from Altrincham, Greater Manchester Published 17 November 2026 A teenager who wants to become an electrician said he had applied for more than 100 apprenticeships without any success. Dawud Hussain, who is studying electrical installation at Tameside College in Greater Manchester, and also works in a barbershop, said most employers did not even respond to his applications. The 18-year-old spoke to BBC Radio Manchester as a major government-commissioned review set out recommendations for reducing the number of Neets (young people who are not in education, employment or training). City region mayor Bev Craig wants more powers to tackle youth unemployment, including plans for a new apprenticeships hub to double the number available. Dawud, who is seeking an apprenticeship starting in September 2027, said that while his college course was going well, finding an opportunity outside the classroom was proving to be very difficult. "It's like you don't get a chance," he said. "It's tough, it's really tough because when you apply for so much and you don't get a reply back..." He said only a couple of employers had spoken to him, while others either rejected his applications or failed to respond. Dawud said he had been working at a barbershop for about two years but "my first choice is being an electrician". Although he is studying and working, Dawud's difficulties securing an apprenticeship illustrate wider concerns about the number of Neets. Nearly a million young people across the UK are in that position. Image caption, Hairdressing apprentice Honey con

title: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents

input.lead: Hundreds of customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire remain without electricity
input.summary: Hundreds of customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire remain without electricity
input.evidence_text: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Properties across Greater Manchester and Lancashire are without power By Angela Ferguson North West Published 17 November 2026 Hundreds of properties in Greater Manchester and Lancashire have been hit by power cuts caused by "unexpected" incidents including underground cables. SP Electricity North West (SPENW) said properties in Oldham, Rochdale, Salford, Blackpool, Lancaster, Myerscough and Bilsborrow and North Meols had been affected. SPENW apologised for the disruption, saying that about 279 properties in Myerscough and Bilsborrow in Lancashire had since been reconnected. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies," said a spokesperson. In Saddleworth, Oldham, 191 properties continue to be affected, with SPENW preparing to send a team out to investigate. In Cadishead and Lower Irlam in Salford, 126 properties are without electricity, with engineers already on site. In the Clifton area of Blackpool, 60 properties are cut off, with engineers en route. In Whalley in the Ribble Valley, 244 properties remain cut off. And in North Meols in West Lancashire, 119 properties are affected, with SPENW preparing to send a crew out. A spokesperson said: "We are aware of separate power cuts affecting properties in parts of Lancashire and Greater Manchester due to faults on the underground electricity network. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies, and we apologise for the disruption caused." title: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says

input.lead: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
input.summary: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
input.evidence_text: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says - BBC News Image caption, Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham has been used to house male asylum seekers since November 2024 By Kevin Fitzpatrick , Greater Manchester political reporter and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 17 November 2026 A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said. Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel". The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning". A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites". Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Anti-immigration protesters gathered outside the hotel in August last year Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers. "It's bad news for community, bad news for taxpayers, and bad news for people themselves seeking asylum. "It's a practice that should never have been started." Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say

input.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
input.summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
input.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 17 November 2026 Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. title: LCD Soundsystem to headline Platt Fields Park gigs in 2027

input.lead: The Manchester park will host a series of 25,000-capacity concerts over two weekends next summer
input.summary: The Manchester park will host a series of 25,000-capacity concerts over two weekends next summer
input.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

John Graveson moved alongside the excavator before continuing behind it As John Graveson passed behind the excavator, Horan placed the vehicle into reverse and began manoeuvring backwards. input.evidence_text: Newhey in the borough of Rochdale is the type of Pennine village that comes into its own this time of year. In late Autumn, its soot-painted, limestone terraced cottages sit huddled against the frosting air. Dew-covered hills lie at both ends of the main street The Bird in Hand pub has been shut since the summer of 2018.
